A volume entry without a source becomes a project-labelled volume <project>_<service>_anon-<10 hex> with a unique name, filled from the image's content at the target (copy-up) by a helper container. Recreating an existing container (a changed configuration, --force-recreate) mounts the volume that container used; a container created because none existed gets a new volume and the old one is left in place, as Docker does. Nothing is deleted implicitly: down -v removes every project-labelled anonymous volume, orphans included; if the copy fails only the volume just created is removed and up exits 1. The same marker/recreate/up -V/down+up sequence runs against Docker in the conformance tier (test_conformance_fixtures.ConformanceFixtureTests.test_fixture_s_anonymous_volumes_follow_the_container_and_are_never_deleted_implicitly).
